reference: GNU coreutils tty independently checks non-terminal stdin, -s and argument parsing. Bash type/help metadata follow the documented tty [-s] interface. Successful PTY output remains deferred.
coverage: Default output and status when stdin is not a terminal.
Silent mode status, repeated -s options, and -- option termination with non-terminal stdin.
Non-terminal detection when stdin is redirected from a relative regular fixture file.
Invalid option diagnostics/status and extra-operand validation, including with -s.
Bash type and help metadata: configured short help and the documented command description.
Successful ttyname(0) behavior is recorded as deferred because the runner does not provide PTY-attached stdin.
exclusions: Successful terminal-name output and -s success require stdin attached to a PTY; no such input fixture is available in this runner.
Terminal paths vary with the PTY allocator, so a future PTY case must provide the same isolated PTY setup to both reference and candidate arms.

cases.purpose: GNU tty prints the documented fallback text and returns failure when standard input is not a terminal.
The -s option suppresses output while preserving the non-terminal failure status.
Repeated short silent options are accepted and remain silent for non-terminal stdin.
A standalone -- ends option parsing without changing the no-operand non-terminal result.
A relative regular file redirected to stdin is not reported as a terminal; tree comparison also checks that the fixture input is unchanged.
An unsupported short option is rejected with the GNU tty usage-error status and a diagnostic; diagnostic wording is allowed to differ.
GNU tty rejects an extra operand instead of treating it as an option to ignore.
The silent flag does not make an invalid extra operand valid; GNU tty still reports a usage error.
Bash type -t must identify the statically registered tty command as a builtin.
Bash help exposes the documented tty [-s] synopsis; metadata only.
Bash help includes the stock tty documentation's first description line, 'Display terminal name.'
cases.script: help_text=$(help tty); case "$help_text" in *"Display terminal name."*) printf 'Display terminal name.\n' ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac

cases.purpose: Exercise successful terminal-name reporting and -s success with stdin attached to a real pseudo-terminal.
cases.reason: The harness always launches fixtures with stdin=/dev/null and has no PTY attachment option. A future disposable VM or PTY-capable mock must create an isolated PTY, attach the same slave to fd 0 for both GNU and candidate arms, and assert the emitted terminal path plus silent-mode success.
